summary: Seychelles says there are no visa requirements for any traveller — all visitors receive a Visitor's Permit on arrival for up to three months — but everyone must first obtain the paid Electronic Travel Authorisation online before travelling.

fee.notes: Standard processing (24 hours), adults and children 12 and under. Premium processing (6 hours) is €30; expedited processing (60 minutes) is €70 for adults and €30 for children. Bank charges are not included.

fee.notes: Charged for each additional period of up to three months, or part of one, after the first three months, which are free; the permit can be extended to twelve months in total. Apply online at permits.ics.gov.sc and pay by card, or in person at Independence House, Victoria.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: Travellers aged 1 to 59 must upload a yellow fever vaccination certificate only if they are travelling from a country or region where the disease is endemic; a transit of less than 12 hours through an airport in such a region does not count. Travellers aged 60 and over need not submit one.

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for Seychelles.

source.name: Seychelles Electronic Border System — FAQs (Information for Visitors & Tourists)

onwardTicket.text: A valid return or onward ticket for the duration of the visit is one of the conditions for the Visitor's Permit issued on arrival, and must also be shown when applying for the Travel Authorisation.

source.name: Seychelles Immigration and Civil Status — Visitor’s Permit

proofOfFunds.text: Immigration requires proof of sufficient funds to cover the whole stay, together with a return or onward ticket and confirmed accommodation. No minimum amount is published.

source.name: Seychelles Immigration and Civil Status — Visitor’s Permit

currencyLimits.text: Cash of SCR 50,000 or more (or the foreign-currency equivalent) must be declared to Customs on arrival and on departure.

notes: Canada's travel advice says strict regulations may be enforced on the temporary import or export of firearms, spear-fishing equipment, and fruits and vegetables.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says most hotels, restaurants and shops in tourist areas accept debit and credit cards, and that goods and services can be paid for in rupees, euros or US dollars. ATMs at the airport and in the main tourist areas generally issue only rupees, and exchanging money at anything other than the official rate is prohibited.

safety.text: The UK government says crime is generally non-violent, but that break-ins, bag snatching and thefts from parked cars, boats and accommodation occur and people walking at night have been robbed; it advises using a hotel safe for valuables. It says beaches do not always have safety information and that some, including Beau Vallon, may have dangerous rip currents when the sea is rough.

idp.text: Seychelles is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Seychelles is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Seychelles yet.

tips.text: Complete the paid Travel Authorisation at seychelles.govtas.com before you travel: the official site says you may be denied boarding without one and that arriving without one costs a EUR 30 penalty. Standard processing takes 24 hours.

For stays of one night or more, the Travel Authorisation application asks for your hotel or accommodation booking, or a letter of invitation if you stay with family or friends; the official site says applications using accommodation not on the Tourism Department's list of licensed establishments may be denied.

The UK Foreign Office says beaches can be safe at some times of year and dangerous at others: the west coast is generally unsafe during the north-west monsoon (around December to March) and the east coast during the south-east winds (around May to September), and Beau Vallon can have dangerous rip currents when the sea is rough.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Seychelles?
faq.answer: No — Seychelles says there are no visa requirements for any traveller visiting Seychelles. Visitors receive a Visitor's Permit on arrival for up to three months. Before travel, every visitor must obtain the paid Electronic Travel Authorisation.

faq.question: What is the Seychelles Travel Authorisation?
faq.answer: A digital entry clearance applied for at seychelles.govtas.com or in the official e-Border app. Every traveller, children included, must have one. The official site lists the fee by processing speed: for adults €10 (standard, 24 hours), €30 (premium, 6 hours) or €70 (expedited, 60 minutes); for children 12 and under €10, €30 and €30; bank charges are not included. It says you may be denied boarding by your airline without one.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Seychelles?
faq.answer: The Visitor's Permit is issued for the length of your visit, up to three months initially. It can be extended in-country, in stages, up to a maximum of twelve months in total, provided you still have accommodation, funds and an onward ticket.

faq.question: What do I need to show on arrival in Seychelles?
faq.answer: Your approved Travel Authorisation, a passport valid for your stay, a confirmed return or onward ticket, proof of booked accommodation for every night, and evidence of sufficient funds for the whole stay.

faq.question: Do I need vaccinations for Seychelles?
faq.answer: A yellow fever certificate is only required of travellers aged 1 to 59 arriving from a country or region where the disease is endemic; a transit of less than 12 hours through an airport there does not count.
